thesis.what_must_be_true: AI data-center capex must keep pulling leading-edge foundry/logic (GAA), DRAM/HBM and advanced-packaging capacity additions through CY2027; AMAT must convert its raised build plan into shipments at >=50% non-GAAP gross margin and ~40% incremental operating margin; working capital must normalize so FCF converges back toward ~75% of net income; and export-control/tariff regimes must not remove material China demand. If those hold, FY27 revenue of ~$40B and ~$16 non-GAAP EPS with ~$7.9B FCF is achievable.

validated.preview_note: AMAT reports fiscal Q3 (July 26 quarter) after guiding to a step-function ramp: revenue $8.95B +/-$500M and non-GAAP EPS $3.36 +/-$0.20, a 13% sequential jump justified by management's call for >30% calendar-2026 growth in semiconductor equipment. The last two prints beat the revenue midpoint by 2.4% and 3.4% and EPS by ~$0.20; with the CFO having pre-built inventory and logistics capacity, we model another beat — revenue ~$9.15B and non-GAAP EPS ~$3.50, with GAAP EPS higher (~$3.56) on continued strategic-investment marks. Three things matter. First, gross margin: 50%+ must hold at higher volume despite tariffs and expedited logistics; SSG margin >=54.5% keeps the incremental-margin story intact. Second, cash conversion: Q2 CFO of $845M was depressed by a $1.75B working-capital build; Q3 is seasonally AMAT's strongest cash quarter (FY25 Q3 CFO $2.6B) and we expect ~$2.4B, with FCF ~$1.6B — a miss here reopens the overbuild question. Third, and most important for the reaction: the Q4 guide. We expect ~$9.7B midpoint revenue and ~$3.75 EPS; anything below ~$9.2B suggests the ramp is cresting, while $9.6B+ validates a $38B+ FY27 run-rate. Watch DRAM mix (29% last quarter) for HBM confirmation, China share (27%) for export-control risk, and buyback pace as a management-confidence signal. Positioning is heavy after two record quarters, so an in-line quarter with a soft guide likely hurts more than a beat helps.
validated.reasoning: Revenue: guide $8,950 +/-$500; last two quarters beat midpoints by 2.4% and 3.4% amid the AI ramp with supply pre-positioned, so p50 $9,150 (+2.2%). Gross margin: GAAP ~49.9-50.0% (Q1 49.1% -> Q2 49.9% -> volume leverage offset by tariff/logistics costs). Opex grows with the build plan (R&D $1,070, S&M $240, G&A $172), giving GAAP op income $3,088 (33.7%) — ~45% incremental operating margin on the sequential revenue add, consistent with Q1->Q2 flow-through. Other income $250 embeds ~$100M normal interest income plus ~$145M median net strategic-investment gains (H1 ran +$1.17B; AI-linked holdings likely still appreciating, though this is the widest swing factor in GAAP EPS). GAAP tax ~12.8% -> net income $2,851, EPS $3.56 on 800M shares. Non-GAAP bridge: +$25M acquisition items/deal costs (incl. NEXX), -$145M investment gains, +$72M tax effects (SBC normalization, intra-entity, tax on adjustments) -> $2,803M, EPS $3.50, a $0.14 beat consistent with (slightly below) the recent +$0.20 cadence. Cash flow: Q3 is seasonally strong (FY25 Q3 CFO $2,634M); WC build continues but moderates -> CFO $2,400M, capex $760M (H1 $1,281M, ramping), FCF $1,640M. No debt repayment this quarter (the $1.2B 3.30% notes mature April 2027, i.e., fiscal Q2 FY27, which I fund in fq2_27 CFF). Dividends step to $0.53/sh (~$420M); buybacks step up to $550M. Balance sheet rolls forward: cash $6,469M, retained earnings $61,155M, equity ~$25,980M with SBC/issuance in other_equity, liabilities drift to $16,700M on payables/taxes. FY26 sums to $33.8B revenue / $12.59 non-GAAP EPS. FY27 assumes the exit run-rate carries with modest sequential growth ($40.3B, $16.10), FY28-29 decelerate to mid-single-digit growth with wide p10s reflecting semicap cyclicality and China/export-control risk.
